question.:question/problem: Let $f(x,y)=1\left(x^{3}+y^{3}\right).$ Given that $C$ is the path along the curve $y=1x^{2}+2$ for $x\in [-1,2],$ evaluate $\displaystyle\int_C\nabla f\cdot\mathrm{d}\mathbf r.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a piecewise-smooth curve given by the vector function $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b].$ Let $f$ be a differentiable function of two or three variables such that $∇f$ is continuous on $C.$ The fundamental theorem for line integrals states that 

$$
{\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r=f(r(b))-f(r(a)).
$$

We start by parametrizing the curve $C.$ A suitable parametrization is

$$
r(t)=⟨t,t^{2} + 2⟩,\,t\in [-1,2].
$$

Then, the position vectors of the endpoints of the curve are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨-1,3⟩, \\ r(2) & =⟨2,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the fundamental theorem for line integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C\nabla f\cdot\mathrm{d}\mathbf r & =f(r(2))-f(r(-1)) \\ & =f(2,6)-f(-1,3) \\ & =\left(1\left(\left(2\right)^{3}+\left(6\right)^{3}\right)\right)-\left(1\left(\left(-1\right)^{3}+\left(3\right)^{3}\right)\right) \\ & =\left(1\left(224\right)\right)-\left(1\left(26\right)\right) \\ & =198.\end{aligned}
$$
